_comment: Published figures this site reproduces from its own data. Each quote is copied from the text scripts/fetch-evidence.mjs printed from the named URL in CI (audit.yml external-evidence job), on the date and with the SHA-256 given; fetch-evidence.mjs --verify re-checks that each quote still appears there. `ours` names the computation scripts/build-replications.mjs runs; no figure on our side is typed by hand. Rendered into validation.html's static:replications region.

cards.title: How many words the Leeds corpus analyzes
cards.quote: Version 0.4 of the treebank covers 40% of the Quran by word count (30,895 out of 77,429 words).
cards.check: Sum the tokens column of the verse-lengths table.
cards.note: A word here is a written word; our bundled copy of the corpus has one entry per written word, and the count matches exactly.

cards.title: How much of the Qur'an the Leeds treebank covers
cards.quote: Version 0.4 of the treebank covers 40% of the Quran by word count (30,895 out of 77,429 words).
cards.quote2: grammar for chapters 1-8 and 59-114 of the Quran.
cards.check: Sum the tokens column of the verse-lengths table for surahs 1 to 8 and 59 to 114.
cards.note: The release notes say which chapters the treebank covers; counting the words in exactly those chapters here gives the figure they state.

cards.title: The word count in the corpus author's thesis
cards.quote: To measure the accuracy of morphological annotation by random sampling, from the 77,430 words in the Quran, three random non-overlapping samples were collected, with each 1,000 words in size.
cards.check: Sum the tokens column of the verse-lengths table.
cards.note: One word apart. The same thesis also gives 77,429 (PDF p. 75, describing Salih's 2007 analysis of "each of the 77,429 words in the Quran") and reports an analysis "for 67,516 out of 77,430 words" (PDF p. 168); the version 0.4 release notes give 77,429. The passages read do not explain the difference, so this site does not guess at it.
